## Implementation evidence (Gerrit change 1413)

DECLARED FLOOR: Git >= 2.38 (the version that added `git merge-tree --write-tree`).
Single-sourced in `.github/git-version-floor.txt`, mirroring the repo's existing
`.github/module-size-limit.txt` pattern.

ENFORCEMENT (fail, never skip -- per the operator decision):
- `tests/conftest.py::pytest_configure` calls `tests/_git_floor.floor_violation()` and
  raises `pytest.UsageError` on violation. This aborts the WHOLE session before
  collection, so an under-floor client cannot run any test, degraded or otherwise.
  The diagnostic names the required version, the installed version, the capability
  (`git merge-tree --write-tree`) that needs it, and the upgrade path per platform.
- `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` gains a `Git version floor gate` step in the
  pytest job (both lanes: branch-head and the Gerrit Verified lane, since that file is
  the shared reusable workflow). It reads the same file, so CI cannot carry a second
  copy that drifts, and it fails the runner by name before the 60-minute test job.
- Docs state the same floor: README "Requirements" + Install preamble,
  CONTRIBUTING section 1_0, docs/local-dev-env.md "Prerequisite -- Git >= 2.38".

ORACLE: `tests/unit/test_git_version_floor.py` (29 tests). Authored RED-first; the
first run failed on the real absences (no floor file, no CI gate step, no doc
mention, and the suite did NOT refuse an under-floor git). Contents: version parsing
across real `git --version` shapes incl. `2.39.5 (Apple Git-154)` and Debian suffixes;
rejection of malformed floor declarations and unparseable version output; the
diagnostic's required content; an END-TO-END proof that a PATH shim reporting
`git version 2.37.0` makes `pytest` exit non-zero with the diagnostic and with no
"skip" in the output; a REAL `merge-tree --write-tree` capability probe (two divergent
histories merged, union asserted) rather than a version-string inference; and a
consumer-drift check that README / CONTRIBUTING / local-dev-env.md / the CI workflow
all name the declared value.

NON-VACUITY (the 34c2 / 8a5e rot class this ticket exists to avoid):
Two guards are deliberately FAIL-CLOSED and search the whole `tests/` tree for the
capability rather than a pinned file path, so a module split or rename makes them fail
loudly instead of silently scanning nothing:
- `test_the_merge_tree_regressions_are_still_present` -- some test under tests/ must
  still use `git merge-tree` with `--write-tree`.
- `test_no_merge_tree_regression_is_guarded_by_skip_machinery` -- no module holding one
  may contain `pytest.skip(` / `importorskip` / `mark.skip` / `mark.xfail` / `xfail(`.

TEETH (mutation checks, both bit):
- Raised the floor file to 99.0 and ran an UNRELATED module
  (tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py): the run aborted with the full diagnostic,
  proving the enforcement is session-wide and unskippable, not local to one test.
- Dropped a throwaway module containing `merge-tree` + `pytest.skip(` into
  tests/integration/: the no-skip guard went RED and named the offending file.

THE 8185 REGRESSION STILL RUNS EVERYWHERE:
- Executed locally: `pytest tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py
  -k "two_clone_union or enrichment_drain" -rs` -> 5 passed, 0 skipped. That set is
  `test_enrichment_drain_preserves_two_clone_union` (the 8185 regression) plus the three
  sidecar siblings from 55bc-b6bf-7adc-4108.
- Gating CI environments are ubuntu-latest and macos-latest (the `_build-and-test.yml`
  matrix, shared verbatim by the push/PR lane and the Gerrit Verified lane). Both runner
  images ship Git well above 2.38; the new gate step now asserts that explicitly per leg
  and prints the observed version, so a future runner-image regression fails loudly
  instead of silently. The integration tier runs on every matrix leg
  (`pytest -m integration`), and nothing in it is conditionally skipped.
- No skip path exists to fall back to: the floor aborts the session instead.

GATES RUN LOCALLY: make lint (ruff check + format-check + zizmor + actionlint), make
typecheck (mypy, 433 files clean), make config-check, check_comment_hygiene,
check_raw_git_writes, check_wall_clock_asserts, check_docs_index --check,
check_readme_quickstart -- all green. Full default suite: 10253 passed, 46 skipped,
2 failed; both failures reproduce identically with the change stashed, so they are
pre-existing on origin/main and unrelated (grounding coverage reconstruction expecting
a local `opengrep` backend, and an identity-ledger history-rewrite test).

RESIDUAL: the plan-review advisories on file_impact (P9) and compound AC wording (P6)
were both triaged "defer" below their block line and are accepted, not fixed -- editing
the description post-attestation would invalidate the signature for no verification gain.
